title: The Ultimate Family Tree Reveal: From Adam to the Kings
paragraphs: Adam, Seth, and Enosh.
Kenan, Mahalalel, and Jared.
Enoch, Methuselah, and Lamech.
Noah.
Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
Japheth's kids were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
Gomer's kids were Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
Javan's kids were Elisha, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim.
Ham's kids were Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
Cush's kids were Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raamah, and Sabteca.
Raamah's kids were Sheba and Dedan.
Cush was also the father of Nimrod, who was like the first big hero on Earth.
Mizraim was the ancestor of the Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim, Pathrusim, Casluhim, and the Caphtorim (where the Philistines came from).
Canaan was the father of Sidon (his first son) and Heth. He was also the ancestor of the Jebusites, Amorites, Girgashites, Hivites, Arkites, Sinites, Arvadites, Zemarites, and Hamathites.
Shem's crew was Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech.
Arphaxad had Shelah, and Shelah had Eber. Eber had two sons: one was named Peleg, which means 'Division,' because back in his day, the whole world got split up. His brother was Joktan.
Joktan's sons were Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah, Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah, Ebal, Abimael, Sheba, Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab—that's all of Joktan's sons.
So, to recap the three main family lines: Shem, Arphaxad, Shelah, Eber, Peleg, Reu, Serug, Nahor, Terah, and then Abram, who you probably know as Abraham. And Abraham had two sons, Isaac and Ishmael.

Abraham's family tree branched out from there. Ishmael's first son was Nebaioth, then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam, Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. That's the Ishmael side of the family.

Abraham also had kids with Keturah, his concubine. She had Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. Then Jokshan had Sheba and Dedan. And Midian's kids were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. That's the Keturah branch.

Abraham had Isaac, and Isaac had two sons, Esau and Israel (who was also called Jacob). Esau's sons were Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. Eliphaz's sons were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, Kenaz, Timna, and Amalek. And Reuel's sons were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.

Then there was Seir, whose sons were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. Lotan's sons were Hori and Homam, and Timna was Lotan's sister. Shobal's sons were Alian, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam. Zibeon's sons were Aiah and Anah. Anah's son was Dishon. Dishon's sons were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Keran. Ezer's sons were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan. And Dishan's sons were Uz and Aran.
Here's a list of the kings who were in charge in the land of Edom before Israel even had a king:
First up was Bela, son of Beor. His city was Dinhabah.
After Bela died, the next king was Jobab, son of Zerah from Bozrah.
After Jobab died, the next king was Husham from the land of the Temanites.
After Husham died, the next king was Hadad, son of Bedad. This was the guy who beat Midian in Moab. His city was Avith.
After Hadad died, the next king was Samlah from Masrekah.
After Samlah died, the next king was Shaul from Rehoboth-by-the-River.
After Shaul died, the next king was Baal-Hanan, son of Acbor.
After Baal-Hanan died, the next king was Hadad. His city was Pau, and his wife was Mehetabel, who was the daughter of Matred, who was the daughter of Me-Zahab.
And then, finally, Hadad died.

After all that, the chiefs of Edom were Chief Timna, Chief Alvah, Chief Jetheth, Chief Oholibamah, Chief Elah, Chief Pinon, Chief Kenaz, Chief Teman, Chief Mibzar, Chief Magdiel, and Chief Iram. Those were the main chiefs in Edom.

title: The Ultimate Family Tree Reveal
paragraphs: Alright, so here's the rundown of Israel's (aka Jacob's) sons: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.

Okay, so Judah had three sons, Er, Onan, and Shelah, with his wife Bathshua, who was from Canaan. But get this, Judah's first son, Er, was so out of line that God literally just took him out. Then, in a wild turn of events, Judah had two more sons, Perez and Zerah, with his daughter-in-law Tamar. So, five sons for Judah in total. From there, Perez had Hezron and Hamul. Zerah had five sons: Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Darda. Then there was this guy Carmi, whose son Achar messed up big time by breaking a sacred rule and basically cursed all of Israel. Not a good look. Ethan's son was Azariah. And Hezron's sons were Jerahmeel, Ram, and Chelubai.

Ram's son was Amminadab, and his son was Nahshon, who was a big deal in the Judah tribe. Nahshon's line went Salmon, then Boaz, then Obed, then Jesse. Jesse’s firstborn was Eliab, then Abinadab, Shimea, Nethanel, Raddai, Ozem, and finally David, who was the seventh. They had two sisters, Zeruiah and Abigail. Zeruiah had three sons: Abishai, Joab, and Asahel. Abigail had a son named Amasa, and his dad was Jether the Ishmaelite.

Hezron's son Caleb had kids with his wife Azubah and also with Jerioth. Azubah's sons were Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon. After Azubah passed away, Caleb married Ephrath, and they had a son named Hur. Hur's son was Uri, and Uri's son was Bezalel. Later on, when Hezron was 60, he married the daughter of Makir, who was the main guy in Gilead. She had a son named Segub. Segub's son was Jair, who owned 23 cities in Gilead. But then, Geshur and Aram came and took over Jair's villages and Kenath and all their little towns—like 60 of them. All those places originally belonged to Makir's family. After Hezron died, Caleb married his dad's wife Ephrathah, and she had Ashhur, who was the founder of Tekoa.
The sons of Jerahmeel, who was Hezron's firstborn, were: Ram (the oldest), then Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah. Jerahmeel also had another wife named Atarah, and she had a son named Onam.
Ram, Jerahmeel's firstborn, had three sons: Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
Onam's sons were Shammai and Jada.
Shammai's sons were Nadab and Abishur. Abishur's wife was Abihail, and they had two sons, Ahban and Molid.
Nadab had two sons, Seled and Appaim. Seled died without having any kids.
Appaim's son was Ishi, Ishi's son was Sheshan, and Sheshan's son was Ahlai.
Jada, who was Shammai's brother, had two sons, Jether and Jonathan. Jether died without any kids.
Jonathan's sons were Peleth and Zaza.
So yeah, that's the whole family tree for Jerahmeel's descendants.

Sheshan didn't have any sons, just daughters. But he had an Egyptian servant named Jarha. So Sheshan had his daughter marry Jarha, and they had a son named Attai. The family line from there goes: Attai, then Nathan, then Zabad, then Ephlal, then Obed, then Jehu, then Azariah, then Helez, then Eleasah, then Sismai, then Shallum, then Jekamiah, and finally Elishama.
Jerahmeel's brother Caleb had a son, his firstborn, named Mesha. Mesha's son was Ziph, and Ziph's son was Mareshah, who founded Hebron.
Hebron's sons were: Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema. Shema's son was Raham, who founded Jorkeam. Rekem's son was Shammai.
Shammai's son was Maon, and Maon founded Beth Zur.
Caleb's concubine Ephah had three sons: Haran, Moza, and Gazez. Haran also had a son named Gazez.
Jahdai's sons were: Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph.

Caleb had another concubine, Maacah, who had Sheber and Tirhanah. She also had Shaaph, who founded Madmannah, and Sheva, who founded Macbenah and Gibea. Caleb's daughter was Acsah. So that's the Caleb branch of the family tree.
The sons of Hur, who was Ephrathah's firstborn, were: Shobal (who founded Kiriath Jearim), Salma (who founded Bethlehem), and Hareph (who founded Beth Gader).

The family of Shobal, the founder of Kiriath Jearim, included Haroeh, half the people of Manahath, and the families of Kiriath Jearim—the Ithrites, the Puthites, the Shumathites, and the Mishraites. The Zorathites and Eshtaolites also came from this line.

The sons of Salma were: Bethlehem, the Netophathites, Atroth Beth Joab, half of the Manahathites, the Zorites, and the families of Sopherim who lived at Jabez—the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, and the Sucathites. These guys were the Kenites who came from Hammath, the founder of the house of Recab.

title: King David's Family Tree: The Ultimate Royal Lineup
paragraphs: So, here's the rundown on King David's sons, born while he was ruling from Hebron.
First up was Amnon, whose mom was Ahinoam from Jezreel.
Second was Daniel, from Abigail of Carmel.
Third was Absalom, son of Maacah, who was the daughter of King Talmai of Geshur.
Fourth in line was Adonijah, son of Haggith.
Fifth was Shephatiah, son of Abital.
And the sixth was Ithream, from his wife Eglah.
These were the six sons he had in Hebron, where he was king for seven and a half years.

Then he moved to Jerusalem and was king there for another 33 years. In Jerusalem, he had more sons: first Shammua, then Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon. The mother of these four was Bathsheba, the daughter of Ammiel. But wait, there's more! He had another nine sons: Ibhar, Elishua, Eliphelet, Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Eliada, and another Eliphelet. These were all David's sons, and they also had a sister named Tamar. Plus, he had other sons with his concubines.

The family tree keeps going. Solomon's son was Rehoboam, whose son was Abijah, who had Asa, who had Jehoshaphat, who had Jehoram, who had Ahaziah, who had Joash, who had Amaziah, who had Azariah, who had Jotham, who had Ahaz, who had Hezekiah, who had Manasseh, who had Amon, and who had Josiah.
Josiah had a few sons himself. His first was Johanan, then Jehoiakim, then Zedekiah, and the youngest was Shallum.
Jehoiakim’s sons were Jeconiah (also called Jehoiachin) and Zedekiah.
Then Jeconiah had sons while he was a prisoner in Babylon: Shealtiel, Malkiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.
Pedaiah had two sons, Zerubbabel and Shimei. Zerubbabel had Meshullam and Hananiah, and their sister was Shelomith. He also had five more sons: Hashubah, Ohel, Berekiah, Hasadiah, and Jushab-Hesed.
Hananiah's sons were Pelatiah and Jeshaiah. Then there were the sons of Rephaiah, the sons of Arnan, the sons of Obadiah, and the sons of Shecaniah.
Shecaniah had a son named Shemaiah, who had six sons: Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat.
Neariah had three sons: Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam.
And Elioenai had seven sons: Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani.

title: This One Prayer Changed His ENTIRE Life
paragraphs: Alright, so here's the rundown on Judah's crew: Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal. Shobal's son was Reaiah, and Reaiah's sons were Jahath, Ahumai, and Lahad. These guys started the Zorathite families.

Then there were the sons of Etam: Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash, and their sister was named Hazzelelponi. Penuel was the father of Gedor, and Ezer was the father of Hushah. These were all descendants of Hur, who was the first son of Ephrathah, the guy who basically founded Bethlehem.

Ashhur, the founder of Tekoa, had two wives, Helah and Naarah. Naarah had Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari—those were her kids. Helah's sons were Zereth, Zohar, Ethnan, and Koz. Koz was the ancestor of Anub, Hazzobebah, and the families of Aharhel, son of Harum.

Now, check this out: there was this guy Jabez. He was a total legend, way more honorable than his brothers. His mom named him Jabez, which means 'pain,' because she went through a lot when she had him. But Jabez prayed to the God of Israel, and was like, 'Yo, for real, bless me! Give me a ton of land, and please, protect me so nothing bad can happen to me.' And God actually gave him exactly what he asked for. Wild.

Kelub, who was Shuhah's brother, had a son named Mehir. Mehir's son was Eshton, and Eshton's sons were Beth Rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah, who founded Ir Nahash (the 'City of Smiths'). These guys were known as the men of Recah.
The sons of Kenaz were Othniel and Seraiah.
Othniel's sons were Hathath and Meonothai.
Meonothai's son was Ophrah, and Seraiah's son was Joab, who founded Ge Harashim (the 'Colony of Artisans').
The sons of Caleb, Jephunneh's son, were Iru, Elah, and Naam.
Elah's son was Kenaz.
The sons of Jehallelel were Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel.

The sons of Ezrah were Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon. One of Mered's wives was Bithiah, who was Pharaoh's daughter. She had Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah, the founder of Eshtemoa. His other wife, who was from Judah, had Jered, the founder of Gedor; Heber, the founder of Soco; and Jekuthiel, the founder of Zanoah.
The sons of Hodiah's wife, who was Naham's sister, were the father of Keilah the Garmite and Eshtemoa the Maacathite.
The sons of Shimon were Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-Hanan, and Tilon.
The sons of Ishi were Zoheth and Ben-Zoheth.

The sons of Shelah, who was Judah's son, were Er (the founder of Lecah), Laadah (the founder of Mareshah), the family of linen workers at Beth Ashbea, Jokim, the men of Cozeba, and Joash and Saraph, who ruled in Moab and Jashubi Lehem. This is all from super old records, btw. They were the potters who lived at Netaim and Gederah, and they worked for the king.
The Simeon family tree went like this: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul. Shaul's son was Shallum, Shallum's son was Mibsam, and Mibsam's son was Mishma.
Mishma's son was Hammuel, and Hammuel's son was Zaccur, and Zaccur's son was Shimei.

Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters, but his brothers didn't have nearly as many kids, so their family never got as big as Judah's. They lived in a bunch of towns: Beersheba, Moladah, Hazar Shual, Bilhah, Ezem, Tolad, Bethuel, Hormah, Ziklag, Beth Marcaboth, Hazar Susim, Beth Biri, and Shaaraim. They lived there until David became king. They also had five other towns nearby—Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Token, and Ashan—and all the villages around them, all the way to Baalath. That was their territory, and they kept really good family records.

Then there's this list of leaders: Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah son of Amaziah, Joel, Jehu son of Joshibiah (who was the son of Seraiah, son of Asiel), Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah, and Ziza son of Shiphi (who was the son of Allon, son of Jedaiah, son of Shimri, son of Shemaiah). All these guys were leaders in their families. They were super successful and their families grew so much that they had to go all the way to Gedor (Gerar), to the east of the valley, to find enough pasture for their flocks. And they found it—it was amazing pasture, super spacious, peaceful, and quiet.

Some Hamites used to live there, but when Hezekiah was king of Judah, these guys came and attacked them, wrecking their tents and houses. There was nothing left of them. Then they just moved in and took over because the land was so good for their flocks. And get this: 500 of these Simeonites, led by Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel (the sons of Ishi), went and invaded the hill country of Seir. They took out all the Amalekites who had escaped and were still hanging around. And they're still living there today.

title: Israel's OG Tribes: Family Drama & Epic Battles
paragraphs: So, here's the story on Reuben's family, Israel's oldest son. Even though Reuben was the firstborn, he totally blew it by hooking up with his dad's concubine. Super messed up, right? So, his firstborn rights got handed over to Joseph's sons. He basically got demoted from being the #1 kid in the family tree. And get this, even though Judah's family line became the most powerful and King David came from them, the official 'firstborn' title still went to Joseph's kids.
The sons of Reuben, Israel's firstborn, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.

The descendants of Joel went like this: Shemaiah, then his son Gog, his son Shimei, his son Micah, his son Reaiah, his son Baal, and his son Beerah. This guy Beerah was the leader of the Reubenites, but he got captured and taken away by Tiglath-Pileser, the king of Assyria.

Beerah's relatives are all listed in the family records by their clans: first Jeiel, then Zechariah, and then Bela son of Azaz, who was the son of Shema, who was the son of Joel. Joel's crew lived in the area from Aroer all the way to Nebo and Baal Meon. Their family owned land right up to the edge of the desert that stretches to the Euphrates River because their herds of animals got so huge they couldn't all fit in Gilead. During King Saul's time, they went to war with the Hagrites and won, taking over their camps and living there on the eastern edge of Gilead.
The Gad tribe were their neighbors in Bashan, all the way to Salecah. Joel was their top guy, Shapham was second-in-command, and then there was Janai, who was the judge in Bashan.

Their relatives, listed by families, were Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber—seven of them. These were the sons of Abihail, who was the son of Huri, son of Jaroah, son of Gilead, son of Michael, son of Jeshishai, son of Jahdo, son of Buz. Ahi, son of Abdiel, who was the son of Guni, was the head of their family.
The Gad family lived in Gilead and Bashan, including the nearby towns, and their land went all the way to the pastures of Sharon.
They were all officially registered in the family tree when Jotham was king of Judah and Jeroboam was king of Israel.

The families of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh had 44,760 guys ready for war—they were all fit and knew how to use a shield, sword, and bow. They went up against the Hagrites, Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab. God had their backs while they were fighting. He basically handed the Hagrites and all their allies over to them because they cried out to him for help during the battle. God came through for them because they trusted him. They took a ton of their stuff: 50,000 camels, 250,000 sheep, and 2,000 donkeys. They also captured 100,000 people. A lot of people died, because it was God's battle. They lived in that land until they were exiled.

The half-tribe of Manasseh had a huge population. They lived in the land from Bashan to Baal Hermon, that is, to Senir (Mount Hermon). The leaders of their families were Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel—they were all brave warriors, super famous, and leaders of their families. But they weren't loyal to the God of their ancestors. They started worshipping the fake gods of the people who lived in the land before them, the ones God had gotten rid of. So the God of Israel made Pul, the king of Assyria (who was also Tiglath-Pileser), come and take the families of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh into exile. He deported them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the Gozan river. And they've been there ever since.

title: The Levites: God's OG Worship Crew
paragraphs: Alright, so Levi's sons were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. Kohath's crew included Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. Amram's kids? The famous trio: Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. Aaron's sons were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. Then it's a whole family tree situation: Eleazar was Phinehas's dad, Phinehas was Abishua's dad, Abishua was Bukki's dad, Bukki was Uzzi's dad, Uzzi was Zerahiah's dad, Zerahiah was Meraioth's dad, Meraioth was Amariah's dad, Amariah was Ahitub's dad, Ahitub was Zadok's dad, Zadok was Ahimaaz's dad, Ahimaaz was Azariah's dad, Azariah was Johanan's dad, and Johanan had Azariah—the one who was the priest in the temple Solomon built in Jerusalem, which was a pretty big deal. After him, the line went Azariah, then Amariah, Ahitub, Zadok, Shallum, Hilkiah, Azariah, Seraiah, and finally Jehozadak.
So, Jehozadak was the one who got hauled off into exile when God used Nebuchadnezzar to take Judah and Jerusalem away.

Okay, let's break down the Levi fam again. Levi's sons: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimei. Kohath's sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. These were the main Levitical clans, family by family. For Gershon's line, you had his son Libni, then his son Jehath, then Zimmah, Joah, Iddo, Zerah, and Jeatherai. For Kohath's line, it was his son Amminadab, then Korah, Assir, Elkanah, Ebiasaph, Assir again, Tahath, Uriel, Uzziah, and Shaul. Elkanah's sons were Amasai and Ahimoth. Then that line went Elkanah, Zophai, Nahath, Eliab, Jeroham, and another Elkanah. The prophet Samuel's sons were Joel, the oldest, and Abijah, the second. Merari's line went Mahli, his son Libni, his son Shimei, his son Uzzah, his son Shimea, his son Haggiah, and his son Asaiah.

These were the guys King David put in charge of the music ministry at the house of God after they brought the Ark of the Covenant there. They were basically the worship leaders at the place of worship, the Tent of Meeting, until Solomon built the actual Temple in Jerusalem. They took their jobs seriously and followed all the instructions they were given.

Here's the lineup of the main worship leaders and their sons who helped out. From the Kohathite family, you had Heman, the head choirmaster. His family tree is also super long, going all the way back to Levi, who was a son of Israel himself: he was the son of Joel, who was the son of Samuel, son of Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Eliel, son of Toah, son of Zuph, son of Elkanah, son of Mahath, son of Amasai, son of Elkanah, son of Joel, son of Azariah, son of Zephaniah, son of Tahath, son of Assir, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah, son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, son of Israel.

Heman's right-hand man was Asaph. His family tree is also listed, tracing back to Gershon, another one of Levi's sons. Asaph was the son of Berekiah, son of Shimea, son of Michael, son of Baaseiah, son of Malkijah, son of Ethni, son of Zerah, son of Adaiah, son of Ethan, son of Zimmah, son of Shimei, son of Jahath, son of Gershon, son of Levi.

And from the Merari family, the guys who stood on the left side, was Ethan. He was the son of Kishi, son of Abdi, son of Malluch, son of Hashabiah, son of Amaziah, son of Hilkiah, son of Amzi, son of Bani, son of Shemer, son of Mahli, son of Mushi, son of Merari, son of Levi.
The rest of the Levites were given all the other jobs that needed to be done in the house of God.

Aaron and his sons were in charge of the sacrifices on the Altar of Burnt Offering and the Altar of Incense. They handled everything related to the Most Holy Place. They made things right for Israel, just like Moses, God's servant, had commanded.

And here are Aaron's descendants: his son Eleazar, his son Phinehas, his son Abishua, his son Bukki, his son Uzzi, his son Zerahiah, his son Meraioth, his son Amariah, his son Ahitub, his son Zadok, and his son Ahimaaz.

These are the places where the priestly families were given to live. The first pick went to the sons of Aaron from the Kohathite family. They got Hebron in Judah and the fields around it. But the fields and villages farther out went to Caleb, son of Jephunneh. Aaron's family also got the special 'cities of refuge' with their fields: Hebron, Libnah, Jattir, Eshtemoa, Hilen, Debir, Ashan, and Beth Shemesh. From the tribe of Benjamin, they got Geba, Alemeth, and Anathoth, with their fields. All in all, the Kohathite families got thirteen cities. The rest of the Kohathites got ten more cities from the half-tribe of Manasseh. The Gershon families got thirteen cities from the tribes of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and Manasseh in Bashan. The Merari families were given twelve cities from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun. So the Israelites gave the Levites these cities and their fields. They also gave out cities from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin by drawing lots. Some of the Kohath families got their cities from the tribe of Ephraim, including the city of refuge Shechem in the hill country, plus Gezer, Jokmeam, Beth Horon, Aijalon, and Gath Rimmon, all with their fields. The rest of the Kohathites got Aner and Bileam with their fields from the half-tribe of Manasseh. The Gershon families got Golan in Bashan and Ashtaroth from the half-tribe of Manasseh; Kedesh, Daberath, Ramoth, and Anem from the tribe of Issachar; Mashal, Abdon, Hukok, and Rehob from the tribe of Asher; and Kedesh in Galilee, Hammon, and Kiriathaim from the tribe of Naphtali. The rest of the Merari families got Rimmono and Tabor from the tribe of Zebulun; Bezer in the desert, Jahzah, Kedemoth, and Mephaath from the tribe of Reuben on the east side of the Jordan; and Ramoth in Gilead, Mahanaim, Heshbon, and Jazer from the tribe of Gad. All these towns came with their fields.

title: The Ultimate Family Tree Reveal
paragraphs: First up, Issachar's crew. He had four sons: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron. Tola's sons were Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Samuel—all leaders of their family groups. Back when David was king, the Tola family line had 22,600 legit warriors. Uzzi's son was Izrahiah, and his sons were Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah—five brothers, all of them leaders. Their family tree had 36,000 warriors, mostly 'cause they had way more wives and kids than their relatives. All in all, the whole Issachar clan had 87,000 warriors listed in their family records.

Next, Benjamin's family. He had three sons: Bela, Beker, and Jediael. Bela had five sons: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri. All of them were leaders and total fighters, with 22,034 people in their family line. Beker's sons were Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth. Through these leaders, their family tree listed 20,200 warriors. Jediael’s son was Bilhan, and Bilhan's sons were Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Kenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar—all sons of Jediael and family leaders. They had 17,200 warriors ready for a fight. Shuppim and Huppim were Ir's sons, and the Hushim crew came from Aher's family.
Naphtali's sons were Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum. They're listed through their grandma Bilhah's side of the family, who was their grandpa's other wife.

Manasseh's sons, from his Aramean concubine, were Asriel and Makir, who was Gilead's dad. Makir found a wife from the Huppites and Shuppites. His sister's name was Maacah. Another son, Zelophehad, only had daughters, which was kinda unusual. Makir’s wife Maacah had a son she named Peresh. His brother was Sheresh, and his sons were Ulam and Rakem. Ulam's son was Bedan. So that's the family line of Gilead, son of Makir, son of Manasseh. His sister Hammoleketh had three sons: Ishdod, Abiezer, and Mahlah. The sons of Shemida were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.

Ephraim's sons were Shuthelah, then his son Bered, his son Tahath, his son Eleadah, his son Tahath, his son Zabad, and his son Shuthelah. Then there were Ezer and Elead, who were basically cattle thieves. They got killed during a raid by the local guys from Gath. Their dad, Ephraim, was super sad for a long time, and his family came to cheer him up. After that, he and his wife had another kid, a son. He named him Beriah, which means 'Unlucky,' because of all the bad stuff that had happened to his family. His daughter was Sheerah, and she was a builder—she built Lower and Upper Beth Horon and a town called Uzzen Sheerah.

Rephah was Ephraim’s son, and so was Resheph. Telah was his son, then Tahan, then Ladan, then Ammihud, then Elishama, then Nun, and finally, Joshua, his son. They lived in Bethel and the area around it, from Naaran in the east all the way to Gezer and its villages in the west. They also had Shechem and its villages, going as far as Ayyah. Along the borders of Manasseh's territory were Beth Shan, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor, with all their smaller towns. The descendants of Joseph, Israel's son, lived in all these spots.

Asher's sons were Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah, and their sister was Serah. Beriah's sons were Heber and Malkiel, who was the father of Birzaith. Heber had Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and their sister Shua.

Japhlet's sons were Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath. His brother Shomer had Rohgah, Hubbah, and Aram. His other brother Helem had Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal. Zophah's sons were Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah, Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera. Jether's sons were Jephunneh, Pispah, and Ara. Ulla's sons were Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia. These were all Asher's descendants—all responsible, solid men with great character, and brave in a fight. They were all good leaders. Their family tree listed 26,000 men ready for combat.

title: Benjamin's Family Tree is WILD 🤯
paragraphs: Alright, so here's the deal with Benjamin's family. His first son was Bela, then Ashbel, Aharah, Nohah, and Rapha—five boys total. Bela's sons were Addar, Gera, Abihud, Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah, Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram. That's a big family right there.
These are the families of Ehud who lived in Geba but got exiled to Manahath. We're talking Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera. Gera was the one who led them out, and he had two sons, Uzza and Ahihud.

Over in Moab, this guy Shaharaim had kids after divorcing his wives Hushim and Baara. With his new wife Hodesh, he had Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcam, Jeuz, Sakia, and Mirmah. These sons all became leaders of their own families. From his first wife Hushim, he had Abitub and Elpaal. Elpaal's sons were Eber, Misham, and Shemed, and they were the ones who built the towns of Ono and Lod and all the villages around them.

Beriah and Shema were family bosses who lived in Aijalon, and they kicked out the people living in Gath. Their brothers were Shashak and Jeremoth. Beriah's sons were Zebadiah, Arad, Eder, Michael, Ishpah, and Joha. Elpaal's sons were Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber, Ishmerai, Izliah, and Jobab. Shimei's sons were Jakim, Zicri, Zabdi, Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel, Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath. Shashak's sons were Ishpan, Eber, Eliel, Abdon, Zicri, Hanan, Hananiah, Elam, Anthothijah, Iphdeiah, and Penuel. Jeroham's sons were Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah, Jaareshiah, Elijah, and Zicri. These guys were all major family leaders, and they lived in Jerusalem.

Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, lived in Gibeon, and his wife's name was Maacah. His first son was Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab, Gedor, Ahio, Zeker, and Mikloth. Mikloth had a son named Shimeah. They all lived near their relatives in Jerusalem.

Ner had Kish, Kish had Saul (yeah, *that* King Saul), and Saul had Jonathan, Malki-Shua, Abinadab, and Esh-Baal. Jonathan's son was Merib-Baal, and Merib-Baal's son was Micah. Micah's sons were Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz. Ahaz had Jehoaddah, and Jehoaddah had Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri had Moza, and Moza had Binea. Raphah was his son, Eleasah was his son, and Azel was his son. Azel had six sons: Azrikam, Bokeru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. His brother Eshek's sons were Ulam (the firstborn), Jeush, and Eliphelet. Ulam's sons were total warriors, legit amazing archers. They had a huge number of sons and grandsons—like, at least 150. All these people were part of Benjamin's massive family tree.

title: Jerusalem's OG Crew Is Back
paragraphs: Alright, so here’s the complete family history for all of Israel, which was written down in the official records of the Kings of Israel and Judah. This happened back when they were kicked out and sent to Babylon because they were being unfaithful and disobedient.
The first Israelites to bounce back from exile and return to their homes and cities were the priests, the Levites, and the temple support staff.

Here's the lineup of people from the families of Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh who came back to Jerusalem: First up, Uthai son of Ammihud (who was the son of Omri, son of Imri, son of Bani), from the line of Perez, who was Judah's son. From the Shilonite crew, there was Asaiah the firstborn and his sons. From Zerah’s family, there was Jeuel. The whole Judah group was 690 people deep.

From the tribe of Benjamin, there was Sallu son of Meshullam (son of Hodaviah, son of Hassenuah), and Ibneiah son of Jeroham, and Elah son of Uzzi (son of Micri), and Meshullam son of Shephatiah (son of Reuel, son of Ibnijah). The Benjamin group had 956 people. All these guys were the heads of their families.

From the priests, there were Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, and Jakin. Then there was Azariah son of Hilkiah (son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub), who was basically the manager of God's house. There was also Adaiah son of Jeroham (son of Pashhur, son of Malkijah), and Maasai son of Adiel (son of Jahzerah, son of Meshullam, son of Meshillemith, son of Immer). The priests, all leaders of their families, numbered 1,760. They were super skilled and experienced servants in the work of worshipping God.

From the Levites, there was Shemaiah son of Hasshub (son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah), a Merarite. Then there was Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah son of Mica (son of Zicri, son of Asaph). Also, Obadiah son of Shemaiah (son of Galal, son of Jeduthun). And finally, Berekiah son of Asa (son of Elkanah), who lived in the villages of the Netophathites.

The security guards were Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their brothers. Shallum was the chief, and he was the guard at the King’s Gate on the east side. They also worked as security for the Levite family camps.

Shallum son of Kore (son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah), along with his brothers from the Korahite family, were in charge of the worship services, acting as doorkeepers for the Tent. It was just like how their ancestors had guarded the entrance to God's camp. Way back in the day, Phinehas son of Eleazar was in charge of the security guards—God was with him! Now, Zechariah son of Meshelemiah was the security guard at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. The total number of chosen security guards was 212, and they were all officially registered in their own camps. David and Samuel the seer handpicked them because they were super dependable. They and their sons had the permanent job of guarding the gates of God's house, the house of worship. The main security guards were posted at the four entrances—east, west, north, and south. Their brothers in the villages were scheduled to relieve them weekly. The four main guards were responsible for 24/7 surveillance.

Since they were Levites, they were also responsible for the security of all the supplies and valuable stuff in God's house. They stayed up all night on watch and had the key to open the doors every morning. Some of them were in charge of the items used in the Temple worship—they counted everything when it was brought in and taken out. Others were in charge of the sanctuary supplies—flour, wine, oil, incense, and spices. Some of the priests were assigned to mix the oils for the perfume. A Levite named Mattithiah, the firstborn son of Shallum the Korahite, was responsible for baking the bread for the worship services. Some of their brothers, the sons of the Kohathites, were assigned to prepare the bread that was set out on the table every Sabbath.

And then you had the musicians, who were all heads of Levite families. They had their own permanent apartments in the Temple. Because they were on duty 24/7, they didn't have to do any other jobs. These were the heads of the Levite families, listed according to their family tree. They all lived in Jerusalem.

Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, lived at Gibeon, and his wife's name was Maacah. His firstborn son was Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab, Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth. Mikloth was the father of Shimeam. They lived in the same neighborhood as their relatives in Jerusalem.

Ner was the father of Kish, Kish was the father of Saul, and Saul was the father of Jonathan, Malki-Shua, Abinadab, and Esh-Baal. Merib-Baal was Jonathan's son, and Merib-Baal was the father of Micah. Micah's sons were Pithon, Melech, and Tahrea. Ahaz was the father of Jarah, Jarah was the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri was the father of Moza, Moza was the father of Binea, Rephaiah was his son, Eleasah was his son, and Azel was his son. Azel had six sons: Azrikam, Bokeru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan—these were the sons of Azel.

title: King Saul's Epic Fail & Tragic End
paragraphs: So the Philistines went to war with Israel, and the Israelite soldiers totally bailed, running for their lives. But they got slaughtered on Mount Gilboa.

The Philistines were laser-focused on Saul and his sons, and they ended up killing Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malki-Shua. The battle got super intense for Saul—the archers spotted him and he got seriously wounded. He told his armor-bearer, "Yo, pull out your sword and finish me off. I'm not about to let these guys capture me and make a joke out of me."

But his guy was too scared and respected him too much, so he wouldn't do it. So Saul just took his own sword and fell on it. That was the end for Saul. When the armor-bearer saw Saul was dead, he freaked out and did the same thing to himself.

So Saul and his three sons—all four of them—died on the same day. When the Israelites who lived in the valley saw that their army had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their towns and ran. The Philistines just came in and took over.

The next day, when the Philistines were looting the bodies, they found Saul and his sons dead on Mount Gilboa. They stripped Saul's body, chopped off his head, took his armor, and basically sent it on a victory tour around Philistia to show off to their idols and people. They put his armor in their god's temple and stuck his skull in the temple of Dagon like a trophy.

When the people of Jabesh Gilead heard what the Philistines did to Saul, all their best fighters took action. They went and got the bodies of Saul and his sons, brought them back to Jabesh, buried them under the big oak tree there, and mourned for seven days.

Here's what happened: Saul died because he was disobedient to God. He didn't follow God's instructions. Instead of praying, he went to a psychic to get advice. And because he didn't turn to God for help, God took his life and handed the kingdom over to David, Jesse's son.

title: David's Dream Team: The OG Avengers
paragraphs: So basically, all of Israel gathered to meet David at Hebron. They were like, “Yo, look at us. We’re your family, for real.” For a while now, even when Saul was king, you were the one actually calling the shots for Israel. God even said, ‘You’re gonna lead my people Israel; you’re the one who’s gonna be their ruler.’ So when all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, David made a pact with them with God as their witness. Then they officially made David the king of Israel, just like God had said through Samuel.

David and his whole crew went to Jerusalem (which used to be called Jebus, where the Jebusites lived). The people of Jebus told David, “Nah, you can’t come in here.” But David went in anyway and took over the fortress of Zion, which became the City of David. David had announced, “The first person to take down a Jebusite will be my commander-in-chief.” Joab, son of Zeruiah, was the first to do it, so he became the top commander.

David moved into the fortress city, and that’s why it’s called the “City of David.” He built up the city’s defenses all around, including the outer walls (the Millo). Joab rebuilt the city gates. David just kept getting stronger and more influential—the God of Angel Armies was with him!

Now, let’s talk about the leaders of David’s Mighty Men, the guys who had his back when he became king, with all of Israel supporting him, making him king just like God said would happen. Here’s the list of David’s fighting crew:
Jashobeam, son of Hacmoni, was the leader of the Thirty. This man single-handedly took out three hundred men in one battle. No one else came close.

Next up was Eleazar, son of Dodai the Ahohite, one of the top three Mighty Men. He was with David at Pas Dammim when the Philistines gathered for battle. It was in a barley field. The Israelite army started to run away from the Philistines, but then Eleazar and his guys made a stand right in that field—and totally turned the fight around! They destroyed the Philistines, with God’s help—it was a huge victory.

One time, the top three from the Thirty went down a rocky path to meet David at the Cave of Adullam while a group of Philistines was camped in the Valley of Rephaim. David was hiding out in the cave while the Philistines were set up for battle in Bethlehem. David suddenly got a craving and said, “Man, I’d do anything for a drink of water from the well in Bethlehem, the one by the gate!” So the Three snuck into the Philistine camp, got water from the well at the Bethlehem gate, carried it all the way back, and brought it to David. But then David wouldn’t drink it! He poured it out as an offering to God, saying, “God forbid I drink this! It would be like drinking the blood of these men—they risked their lives to get it.” So he refused to drink it. This is the kind of wild stuff the top three Mighty Men did.

Abishai, Joab’s brother, was the leader of the Thirty. He single-handedly fought and killed three hundred men, but he wasn't part of the top Three. He was super respected by the Thirty—he was their leader—but he still wasn't on the same level as the top Three.

Benaiah, son of Jehoiada, was a powerhouse from Kabzeel who did a ton of epic things: he killed two famous Moabite warriors; he went down into a pit on a snowy day and killed a lion; and he took down an Egyptian giant who was seven and a half feet tall. The Egyptian had a spear as big as a ship’s mast, but Benaiah went after him with just a club, snatched the spear out of the Egyptian’s hand, and killed him with it. These are some of the legendary things Benaiah did. But he was never counted among the top Three. He was highly respected among the Thirty, but he just didn't make the cut for the top Three. David put him in charge of his personal bodyguards.

The Mighty Men of the army were: Asahel, Joab’s brother, Elhanan son of Dodo from Bethlehem, Shammoth the Harorite, Helez the Pelonite, Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite, Abiezer the Anathothite, Sibbecai the Hushathite, Ilai the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite, Heled son of Baanah the Netophathite, Ithai son of Ribai from Gibeah of Benjamin, Benaiah the Pirathonite, Hurai from the Gaash ravines, Abiel the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Baharumite, Eliahba the Shaalbonite, the sons of Hashem the Gizonite, Jonathan son of Shagee the Hararite, Ahiam son of Sacar the Haranite, Eliphal son of Ur, Hepher the Mekerathite, Ahijah the Pelonite, Hezro the Carmelite, Naarai son of Ezbai, Joel brother of Nathan, Mibhar son of Hagri, Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Berothite, who was the armor-bearer for Joab son of Zeruiah, Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite, Uriah the Hittite, Zabad son of Ahlai, Adina son of Shiza the Reubenite, who was the Reubenite chief of the Thirty, Hanan son of Maacah, Joshaphat the Mithnite, Uzzia the Ashterathite, Shama and Jeiel the sons of Hotham the Aroerite, Jediael son of Shimri, his brother Joha the Tizite, Eliel the Mahavite, Jeribai and Joshaviah the sons of Elnaam, Ithmah the Moabite, Eliel, Obed, and Jaasiel the Mezobaite.

title: David's GOATED Dream Team Assembles
paragraphs: So, here's the crew that joined David back when he was hiding out in Ziklag. This was during the time he was basically kicked out by King Saul, son of Kish. These guys were total legends, legit warriors.
They were stacked with bows and could sling stones and shoot arrows with either their right or left hand—naturally ambidextrous. They were actually from Saul's own tribe, Benjamin.

First up was Ahiezer, then Joash son of Shemaah the Gibeathite. You also had Jeziel and Pelet, the sons of Azmaveth; Beracah; Jehu the Anathothite; Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, who was a big deal among the Thirty and their leader; Jeremiah; Jahaziel; Johanan; Jozabad the Gederathite; Eluzai; Jerimoth; Bealiah; Shemariah; Shephatiah the Haruphite; Elkanah; Isshiah; Azarel; Joezer; Jashobeam; the Korahites; and Joelah and Zebadiah, the sons of Jeroham from Gedor.

Then you had these Gadites who left their old crew and rolled up to David's fortress in the middle of nowhere. They were straight-up battle-hardened pros who knew their way around a shield and spear. They looked fierce, like lions, but moved incredibly fast, like gazelles racing across the hills. Ezer was the top guy, then Obadiah, Eliab, Mishmannah, Jeremiah, Attai, Eliel, Johanan, Elzabad, Jeremiah, and Macbannai—eleven of them. These guys from Gad were elite—one of them could take on a hundred regular soldiers, and their top guy was worth a thousand. They were the ones who crossed the Jordan River when it was flooding in the first month, and they sent everyone in the lowlands running, east and west.

Some guys from the tribes of Benjamin and Judah also came to join David at his fortress. When David went out to meet them, he was straight up: 'Aight, if you're here to help and not start drama, you're welcome to join the team. But if you're here to snake me out to my enemies, even though I've done nothing wrong, God's gonna see it and you'll get what's coming to you.'
Just then, Amasai, the chief of the Thirty, got hyped by God's Spirit and said,
'We're on your side, David! We're with you, son of Jesse! It's all good with you, and it's all good with whoever helps you. For real, your God has got your back.'
So David welcomed them and made them commanders in his raiding troops.

Some guys from the tribe of Manasseh also switched over to David's side when he was about to go to war against Saul with the Philistines. But in the end, they didn't even fight because the Philistine leaders talked it over and sent them home. They were like, 'Nah, we can't trust these guys with our lives—they'll just betray us to their old boss, Saul.'

The guys from Manasseh who joined David at Ziklag were Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu, and Zillethai—all big-name leaders from Manasseh's families. They helped David with his raids against the desert bandits; they were all tough fighters and great leaders in his crew. It felt like every single day, more people showed up to help. It wasn't long before his crew was so massive it looked like God's own army!

Alright, let's break down the numbers of all the pro fighters who came down from the north to David at Hebron to hand over Saul's kingdom, just like God said would happen: from Judah, carrying shields and spears, 6,800 battle-ready soldiers; from Simeon, 7,100 tough fighters; from Levi, 4,600, which included Jehoiada, the leader of Aaron's family, who brought 3,700 men, and the young, strong Zadok with twenty-two leaders from his family; from Benjamin, Saul's own tribe, 3,000 guys, most of whom had actually stuck with Saul until now; from Ephraim, 20,800 fierce fighters who were famous in their hometowns; from the half-tribe of Manasseh, 18,000 who were chosen to come and make David king; from Issachar, 200 leaders who totally got the times and knew what Israel should do, along with their families; from Zebulun, 50,000 well-equipped veteran warriors who were ride-or-die loyal; from Naphtali, 1,000 chiefs leading 37,000 heavily armed men; from Dan, 28,600 battle-ready men; from Asher, 40,000 veterans, ready for a fight; and from east of the Jordan, from Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, 120,000 heavily armed soldiers.

All these soldiers came to David at Hebron, ready to throw down if needed. They were all on the same page, determined to make David king over all of Israel. And pretty much everyone else in Israel felt the same way—'Make David king!' They all partied with David for three days straight, with their families bringing tons of food and drinks. Neighbors from as far away as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali came with donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen loaded with food for the party: flour, fig cakes, raisin cakes, wine, oil, cattle, and sheep. It was a total vibe in Israel!

title: That Time Moving God's Ark Went SO Wrong
paragraphs: So David got all his leaders together, the big shots in charge of thousands and hundreds of soldiers. Then he pitched this idea to everyone in Israel: "Yo, if you guys are cool with this, and if it's what God wants, let's send out a massive invite. Let's get all our relatives from all over Israel, even the priests and Levites from their towns, to come hang with us. And for real, let's bring back the Ark of our God. It's been collecting dust and totally forgotten ever since Saul was king."

And guess what? The whole assembly was for it. Everyone agreed it was the right move. So David gathered all of Israel, from Egypt's Pond of Horus in the southwest all the way up to the Pass of Hamath in the northeast, to go get the Ark of God from Kiriath Jearim.

Then David and the whole crew went to Baalah (that's Kiriath Jearim) in Judah to bring back the Ark of God. This wasn't just any box; it's the one connected to God's name, the "Cherubim-Throne-of-God." They put the Ark on a brand-new cart they brought from Abinadab's house, with Uzzah and Ahio driving it.

As the Ark of God was moving, David and all of Israel were having a massive worship party. They were singing, dancing, and had a whole marching band with all sorts of instruments. It was a vibe. But when they got to the threshing floor of a guy named Kidon, the oxen pulling the cart stumbled. Uzzah, trying to be helpful, reached out and grabbed the Ark to stop it from falling.

Big mistake. God got seriously angry at Uzzah and struck him dead right there for touching the Ark. He died on the spot, right in front of God. David was ticked off, super angry that God just exploded on Uzzah like that. They even named the place Perez Uzzah, which means "Exploded Uzzah," and it's still called that. David was genuinely terrified of God that day. He was like, "How am I supposed to bring the Ark of God with me now?" So, he called the whole parade off. Instead of taking the Ark to the City of David, he had it stored at the house of a guy named Obed-Edom the Gittite. The Ark of God stayed there for three months, and God totally blessed Obed-Edom's family and everything he owned.

title: David's Epic Wins & God's Wild Game Plan
paragraphs: So, King Hiram from Tyre was like, 'Yo David, let's get you a proper palace.' He sent over a bunch of cedar wood, and some seriously skilled builders. That's when it really hit David—God had totally locked him in as king over Israel. His kingdom was getting famous, and it was all for the good of his people. Oh, and David also married more wives in Jerusalem and had a whole bunch of kids: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Elpelet, Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphelet.

The second the Philistines heard that David was officially king over all of Israel, they showed up in full force to try and capture him. When David got the report, he marched out to handle business. On their way, the Philistines decided to just start trashing the Valley of Rephaim.
David asked God, 'Should I attack the Philistines? Will you give me the win?'
God's answer was straight up: 'Attack. I'll give you the victory.'

So David attacked at this place Baal Perazim and completely crushed them. David said, 'God just exploded on my enemies, like a water pipe bursting!' That's legit how the place got its name, Baal Perazim, which is like 'Baal-Explosion.' The Philistines were so shook they just left their gods there, and David ordered them to be burned.

And then, believe it or not, the Philistines were right back at it, messing things up in the valley again. So David asked God one more time. God replied, 'Okay, new game plan. Don't attack them head-on this time. Circle around and sneak up on them from the balsam grove. When you hear what sounds like footsteps rustling in the treetops, that's your signal to go all out. God will be two steps ahead of you, already out there taking down the Philistine army.'
David did exactly what God told him to do, and he wiped out the Philistines all the way from Gibeon to Gezer.
After that, David's name was known everywhere, far and wide. And God made all the other nations terrified of him.

title: The Ark is FINALLY Coming Home!
paragraphs: After David built a bunch of houses for himself in the City of David, he prepped a special place for the Ark of God and even pitched a tent for it. Then David made it official: “Listen up, no one is allowed to carry the Ark of God except the Levites. God chose them and only them to carry God’s Ark and be on duty 24/7 for worship stuff.”
So David gathered everyone in Israel to Jerusalem to bring the Ark of God up to the spot he had prepared.

David also called for the family of Aaron and the Levites. From Kohath’s family, Uriel the leader with 120 of his relatives; from Merari’s family, Asaiah the leader with 220 relatives; from Gershon’s family, Joel the leader with 130 relatives; from Elizaphan’s family, Shemaiah the leader with 200 relatives; from Hebron’s family, Eliel the leader with 80 relatives; and from Uzziel’s family, Amminadab the leader with 112 relatives.

Then David called in the priests, Zadok and Abiathar, and the Levites—Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab. He told them, “You guys are the heads of the Levite families. You and your relatives need to get yourselves spiritually ready to bring up the Ark of the God of Israel to the place I’ve set up for it. The first time we tried this, you Levites weren’t carrying it right, and God got seriously angry with us because we didn’t do our homework and follow the instructions.”

So the priests and Levites got themselves consecrated and ready to bring up the Ark of the God of Israel. The Levites carried the Ark of God exactly how Moses, following God's direct orders, had commanded. They carried it using poles on their shoulders, making sure not to even touch it with their hands.
David then told the Levite leaders to assign their relatives to the choir, get a full-on marching band together, and just fill the air with happy, loud music.

The Levites assigned Heman son of Joel, and from his family, Asaph son of Berekiah. Then from the Merari family, they assigned Ethan son of Kushaiah. In the second string, they had their brothers: Zechariah, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, and Jeiel, who were on security duty.

The choir and band lineup was: Heman, Asaph, and Ethan rocking the bronze cymbals; Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah were on lyres, playing the main melody; Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah were on harps, playing the harmony; and Kenaniah, the Levite who was basically a musical genius, was the music director.

Berekiah and Elkanah were assigned as porters for the Ark. The priests—Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer—blasted the trumpets in front of the Ark of God. Obed-Edom and Jehiah were also porters for the Ark.

Okay, now they were all set. David, the elders of Israel, and the army commanders headed out to get the Ark of the Covenant of God from Obed-Edom’s house. And they were PUMPED. God was actually helping the Levites, giving them strength as they carried the Ark, so they paused to worship by sacrificing seven bulls and seven rams. Everyone was decked out in fancy linen robes—David, the Levites carrying the Ark, the choir, the band, and Kenaniah the music director. David was also wearing a special linen prayer shawl, called an ephod. The whole crew, all of Israel, paraded up with the Ark of the Covenant of God, shouting, cheering, and playing every kind of instrument you can imagine.

But as the Ark of the Covenant of God was entering the City of David, Saul’s daughter Michal was watching from her window. When she saw King David dancing his heart out, she was disgusted and totally lost respect for him.

title: David Throws a Legit Worship Party
paragraphs: So they brought the Ark of God and set it up right in the middle of the tent David had prepped for it. Then they had a big worship session, giving burnt offerings and peace offerings to God. After David finished with the offerings, he blessed everyone in God's name. Then he handed out snacks to every single person there, guys and girls—a loaf of bread, some BBQ, and a raisin cake. Talk about a feast.

Next, David put some of the Levites on duty in front of the Ark of God to lead the worship. Their job was to pray, give thanks, and just praise the God of Israel. Asaph was the main guy, and under him were Zechariah, Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-Edom, and another Jeiel, who were all on instruments. Asaph was on the drums. The priests Benaiah and Jahaziel were on trumpet duty, blasting them in front of the Ark of the Covenant at scheduled times all day long.
That was the day David officially kicked off regular praise and worship to God, with Asaph and his crew leading the charge.

Give it up for God! Shout out His name! Let the whole world know who He is and the awesome stuff He's done! Sing to Him! Make music for Him! Tell everyone about His amazing works! Get hyped about His holy name; if you're looking for God, be stoked! Focus on God and His power, try to be near Him 24/7. Don't forget all the incredible things He's done, the miracles and the wise judgments He's laid down. You descendants of Israel, His servant! You children of Jacob, His chosen ones! He is the LORD, our God; His rules are literally everywhere. He never forgets His promises, not even after thousands of generations—the deal He commanded, the same one He made with Abraham, the one He swore to Isaac. He made it official for Jacob, an eternal promise for Israel: 'I'm giving you the land of Canaan, it's your inheritance.' And this was when they were just a small group, basically strangers wandering around.

They drifted from one nation to another, from one kingdom to the next. But He didn't let anyone mess with them; He even called out kings for them, saying, 'Don't you dare touch my chosen ones, don't even think about hurting my prophets.'

Sing to God, everyone and everything! Spread the good news of His salvation every single day! Tell all the nations that don't know Him about His glory, tell every person about His amazing deeds. And why? Because God is great—totally worthy of praise! No other god or goddess even comes close. All those popular gods are just fakes, but our God created the entire universe! He's surrounded by splendor and majesty; His place is filled with strength and joy.

Shout 'Bravo!' to God, all you families and nations, be in awe of His glory and strength! Shout 'Bravo!' to His famous name, bring an offering and come hang out with Him! Show up looking sharp in your holy best.

God is the real deal, so take Him seriously. He set the earth in place, and it's not going anywhere. So let the heavens be happy, let the earth celebrate, and spread the word to all nations, 'God is King!' Let the ocean and everything in it roar, let the fields and all their creatures go wild. Then all the trees in the forest will join in, cheering for God—because He's coming to make everything right!

Thank God—He is good and His love is for real, it never stops. Say, 'Save us, God our Savior, gather us up and get us out of these places that don't know you, so we can thank your holy name and just chill in your amazing presence.' Blessed be God, the God of Israel, forever and ever.
Then everyone shouted, 'Yes! Amen!' and 'Praise God!'

David left Asaph and his crew with the Ark of the Covenant of God to be in charge of worship. They were on duty 24/7, taking care of whatever was needed. He also assigned Obed-Edom and his 68 relatives to help out. Obed-Edom, son of Jeduthun, and Hosah were the security guards. The priest Zadok and his priest family were put in charge of the Tent of God at the high place in Gibeon. Their job was to make sure the morning and evening worship services happened every day, with all the proper burnt offerings on the altar, just like God's Law for Israel said. With them were Heman, Jeduthun, and a few others who were specifically picked for the job of 'Give thanks to God, because His love never quits!' Heman and Jeduthun were also decked out with trumpets, cymbals, and other instruments for the worship songs. The sons of Jeduthun were the security team.
Once all the arrangements were set, everyone went home. And David went home to bless his own family.

title: God's Promise to David is Next Level
paragraphs: So after King David got settled in his new place, he said to Nathan the prophet, “Yo, look at this. I’m living it up in this fancy cedar palace, but the Ark of God’s Covenant is just sitting out there in a tent. Kinda messed up, right?”
Nathan replied, “Whatever you’re thinking, man, go for it. God’s totally with you.”

But that night, God’s message came to Nathan. He said, “Go and tell my servant David, this is what God has to say about it: You are NOT the one who’s going to build me a house to live in. I mean, I haven’t lived in a ‘house’ from the day I brought Israel out of Egypt until now. I’ve just been moving from one tent to another. In all my time traveling with Israel, did I ever once say to any of the leaders I appointed, ‘Hey, why haven’t you built me a cedar house?’

“So this is what you need to tell my servant David: The Lord of Heaven’s Armies says: I took you from the fields, from following sheep, and made you the leader of my people Israel. I’ve been with you everywhere you’ve gone and have taken down all your enemies right in front of you. And now, I’m about to make your name famous, like one of the biggest names on earth. I’m going to make a special place for my people Israel and plant them there so they can have their own home and not get pushed around anymore. No more evil people are gonna mess with them like they used to, back when I had judges ruling over them. And I’m going to defeat all your enemies.

“And now I’m telling you: God himself will build YOU a house! When your life is over and you’re with your ancestors, I will raise up your own son to take your place, and I will make his kingdom solid. He’s the one who will build a house for me, and I will make his kingdom last forever. I will be his father, and he will be my son. I will never take my love away from him like I did from the king before you. I will put him in charge of my house and my kingdom forever; his throne will be secure for all time.”
Nathan told David everything he saw and heard in that vision, word for word.
Then King David went in, sat down before God, and prayed:

“Who am I, Lord God, and what is my family, that you’ve brought me this far? But that’s nothing compared to what’s coming. You’ve even talked about my family’s distant future, giving me a peek at what’s ahead and treating me like I’m a big deal, Lord God. What else can I even say about you honoring me like this, when you already know me so well? Lord, because you are so good, you did this amazing thing for me and showed me your incredible plan. There is no one like you, God, and there is no other God but you. We’ve heard it with our own ears. And who is like your people, Israel? They’re the only nation on earth that you went and saved to be your own people. You made your name famous by doing huge, awesome things, driving out other nations and their gods as you rescued your people from Egypt. You made Israel your own people forever. And you, God, became their God.

“So now, God, please make the promise you gave to me and my family last forever! Do exactly what you said! Then your name will be famous and respected forever, and people will say, ‘The Lord of Heaven’s Armies, the God over Israel, is Israel’s God!’ And the family of your servant David will be secure with you. You, my God, told me straight up, ‘I will build you a house.’ That’s what gave me the courage to pray this prayer to you. And since you are God, you have promised all this good stuff to me. And on top of that, you’ve blessed my family so that it will always be in your presence. Because you have blessed it, God, it’s truly blessed—forever!”

title: David's Winning Streak is INSANE
paragraphs: So after that, David went after the Philistines and totally crushed them. He took over their main city, Gath, and all the towns around it.
He also beat Moab in a fight. The Moabites had to start paying David tribute money, basically like a subscription fee to not get attacked again.

Then, as he extended his control to the Euphrates River, David crushed King Hadadezer of Zobah all the way to Hamath. David jacked a thousand of his chariots, seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand foot soldiers. He lamed most of the chariot horses but kept a hundred for himself.

When the Arameans from Damascus rolled up to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David took out twenty-two thousand of them. He set up his own government in Aram-Damascus, and they had to pay him tribute too. God just kept giving David wins everywhere he went.

David also took all the gold shields from Hadadezer's crew and brought them to Jerusalem. And he looted a ton of bronze from Hadadezer's cities, Tebah and Cun. Solomon later used all that bronze to make the Great Bronze Sea, the Pillars, and bronze equipment for the Temple.

When King Tou of Hamath heard that David had crushed the whole army of Hadadezer king of Zobah, he sent his son Hadoram to congratulate David. See, Tou and Hadadezer were major rivals. Hadoram brought David a bunch of cool gifts made of silver, gold, and bronze. King David dedicated all of it to God, along with the stuff he'd already taken from other nations like Edom, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines, and Amalek.
Abishai, who was Zeruiah's son, beat the Edomites in the Valley of Salt—he took down eighteen thousand of them. He set up a government in Edom too, and the Edomites became David's subjects.
God just kept giving David victories, no matter where he went.
So David was the king of all Israel, and he was a really good one. He was fair to everyone and did his job right.
Here's who was on his team:
Joab son of Zeruiah was the army commander;
Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the official record-keeper;
Zadok son of Ahitub and Abimelech son of Abiathar were the priests;
Shavsha was the secretary;
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was in charge of the special forces, the Kerethites and Pelethites;
And David's own sons were his top advisors, super close to him.

title: The Great Beard-Shaving Disaster
paragraphs: So, a while later, King Nahash of the Ammonites passed away, and his son took over the throne. David was like, 'Yo, I should show some love to Hanun, Nahash's son. His dad was always super cool to me.' So, David sent some guys to give his condolences for his dad's passing.

But when David's crew showed up in Ammonite territory to pay their respects to Hanun, the Ammonite leaders were like, 'Bro, are you for real? You actually think David is honoring your dad by sending these guys? Nah, he sent them to spy on our city so he can take it over.'
So Hanun grabbed David's guys, shaved off their beards, chopped their robes in half so their butts were hanging out, and kicked them out.
When David heard what happened, he sent someone to meet his guys because they were totally humiliated. The king was like, 'Just chill in Jericho until your beards grow back, then you can come home.'

When the Ammonites realized they had seriously messed up and David was mad, they spent a fortune—a thousand talents of silver (that's thirty-seven and a half tons!)—to hire chariots and horsemen from the Arameans of Naharaim, Maacah, and Zobah. We're talking 32,000 chariots, plus the king of Maacah and his army. They all camped out at Medeba, and the Ammonites got their own army ready for a fight.
When David got the news, he sent out Joab with his elite troops, ready to go.

The Ammonites marched out and lined up for battle at the city gate. The kings who were their allies set up in the open fields. When Joab saw he was getting attacked from the front and the back, he picked his best soldiers and sent them to fight the Arameans. He put his brother Abishai in charge of the rest of the army to take on the Ammonites. Then he said, 'If the Arameans are too strong for me, you gotta help me out. And if the Ammonites are too much for you, I'll come help you. Be brave! We're fighting for our people and for God's cities. And God's gonna do what he thinks is right.'

But when Joab and his soldiers charged at the Arameans, they totally bailed and ran away. Then the Ammonites saw the Arameans running for their lives, so they bolted too and ran from Abishai back into the city.
So Joab left the Ammonites and went back to Jerusalem.
When the Arameans saw they got crushed by Israel, they regrouped and sent for more of their guys from across the river. Shophach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led them.

When David heard about all this, he gathered all of Israel, crossed the Jordan River, and got ready to fight. The Arameans got into formation, ready for David, and the battle started. But the Arameans scattered again in front of Israel. David took out seven thousand chariot drivers and forty thousand foot soldiers. He also killed Shophach, the army commander. When all the kings who were allied with Hadadezer saw they got beat by Israel, they made peace with David and started serving him. The Arameans were too scared to help the Ammonites ever again.

title: David vs. the Last Giants
paragraphs: So in the spring, the usual time for kings to go to war, Joab took the army out and totally crushed the Ammonites. Then he laid siege to Rabbah. David, meanwhile, was just staying back in Jerusalem. Joab hit Rabbah hard and left it in ruins.

David took the crown right off their king's head. Turns out it weighed a talent of gold and had a sick precious stone in it. They put it on David's head. He also hauled a massive amount of loot from the city and put the people there to work—hard labor with saws, picks, and axes. He did this to all the Ammonite cities. Then David and his whole army went back to Jerusalem.
Later on, another war popped off with the Philistines at Gezer. That's when Sibbecai the Hushathite took down Sippai, who was from the giant clan. The Philistines got totally beaten.
In another battle with the Philistines, Elhanan son of Jair killed Lahmi, the brother of Goliath the Gittite. This dude's spear was huge, like a ship's boom.

And then there was the war at Gath. This one featured a hulking giant who had twenty-four fingers and toes—six on each hand and foot. He was another one from the giant clan. When he started trash-talking Israel, Jonathan, the son of David's brother Shimea, straight up killed him.
These guys were all descendants of the giants in Gath, and they all got taken out by David and his crew.

title: David's Epic Mistake & The Angel with the Sword
paragraphs: So, Satan shows up and talks David into doing a census of Israel. David tells Joab and his army officers, "Go and count everyone in all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba. I wanna know the numbers."

Joab was like, "Dude, for real? May God make his people a hundred times more numerous! They're all your subjects, my king. But why would you do this? You're gonna get Israel in major trouble with God."

But David was stubborn and wouldn't back down. So Joab had to go and do it. He traveled the whole country, came back to Jerusalem, and gave David the numbers: 1,100,000 men who could fight, and Judah had 470,000 of them. Joab was so grossed out by the whole thing that he didn't even count the tribes of Levi and Benjamin. And God was not happy about it at all and punished Israel.
Then David prayed, "I messed up, big time. I chose to trust numbers instead of you. Please forgive me—that was so dumb."
God spoke to David's prophet, Gad, and said, "Go tell David this: 'God's giving you three choices for your punishment. Pick one, and I'll do it.'"

Gad went to David and laid it out: "You want three years of famine, three months of being chased by your enemies, or three days of God's sword—a plague sent by an angel of God? Think about it and tell me what to say to the One who sent me."
David told Gad, "This is all terrible. But I'd rather be punished by God, because his mercy is huge, than be at the mercy of people."

So God sent a plague on Israel, and seventy thousand Israelites died. Then God sent the angel to Jerusalem, but when he was about to start wrecking the place, God felt bad and changed his mind. He told the death angel, "That's enough! Stop!"

The angel of God was right at the threshing floor of a guy named Araunah the Jebusite. David looked up and saw the angel just hanging there between earth and sky, with his sword out, ready to strike Jerusalem. David and the elders just hit the ground, praying and wearing scratchy burlap clothes.
David prayed, "Please! I'm the one who sinned; it's my fault. But these people are like innocent sheep, what did they do? Punish me and my family, not them. Don't take it out on them."
The angel of God told Gad to have David go and build an altar to God on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite. So David did what Gad told him, just like God commanded.

Meanwhile, Araunah had stopped working and was just watching the angel. His four sons freaked out and hid. David walked up to Araunah. When Araunah saw him, he left his threshing floor and bowed down to the king.
David said to Araunah, "Sell me this threshing floor so I can build an altar to God. I'll pay you the full price. We need to stop this plague."

Araunah was like, "My king, just take it! Do whatever you want. Look, I've got an ox for the offering, and you can use the threshing tools for firewood, and here's some wheat for the grain offering—it's all yours!"

David said back, "Nope. I'm buying it from you for the full price. I'm not gonna give God offerings that cost me nothing." So David bought the place from Araunah for six hundred gold coins. He built an altar to God there and made burnt offerings and peace offerings. He called out to God, and God answered by sending fire from the sky to hit the altar. Then God told the angel to put his sword away.
And that's the story of what happened when David saw God answer him on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite when he made the sacrifice.

At that time, the Tabernacle that Moses built in the desert and the Altar of Burnt Offering were at the worship center in Gibeon. But David was too scared of the angel's sword to go there to pray to God.

title: David's Epic Temple Build... But There's a Twist
paragraphs: So David declared, "From now on, this is the site for the worship of God; this is the place for Israel's Altar of Burnt Offering." So David got all the foreigners living in the country together and put them to work. He had them cutting up fancy stones from the quarries to build God's Temple. He also gathered a massive amount of iron for nails and stuff for the gates, so much bronze they couldn't even weigh it all, and a literal forest of cedar logs. Like, the Sidonians and Tyrians sent over massive shipments of cedar just for him.

David was thinking, 'My son Solomon is still a kid, he can't handle all this planning. But this temple for God has to be absolutely epic, something everyone in the world will talk about. So, I'll just get all the materials ready for him.' That's why David went all out and gathered this insane amount of building supplies before he passed away. Then he called Solomon over and was like, 'You're the one who's going to build a temple for the God of Israel.'

David told Solomon, "Son, I really, really wanted to build a temple for my God. But God told me no. He was like, 'You've taken too many lives and fought too many wars. You're not the one to build a temple in my name—you've seen way too much bloodshed. But, you're going to have a son who will be a man of peace. I'll give him a break from all his enemies. His name will even be Solomon, which means 'peace,' and I'll bring peace and quiet to Israel while he's in charge. He's the one who will build a temple for me. He'll be like my own son, and I'll be his father. And I'll make sure his kingdom in Israel lasts forever.'

"So now, my son, I hope God is with you. I hope you crush it and build the temple for your God, just like he said you would. And I pray God gives you the wisdom and understanding you need when he puts you in charge of Israel, so you can rule in reverent obedience under God's Revelation. That's the key to success—just follow the rules and instructions God gave Moses for Israel. Be brave! Take charge! Don't be scared or back down. Look, I've worked so hard to get all this stuff ready for God's temple: 100,000 talents of gold (that's 3,775 tons!) and 1,000,000 talents of silver (that's 37,750 tons!), and so much bronze and iron we can't even weigh it. Plus all this wood and stone. And you can totally add more if you want. You've got tons of skilled workers ready to go: stonecutters, masons, carpenters, and experts in gold, silver, bronze, and iron. You're all set—so get to it! And may God be with you!"

David also ordered all the leaders of Israel to help his son Solomon. He said, "Isn't it obvious that your God is with you? He's given you peace with everyone around you. I did my part by defeating our enemies and taking control of the land for God and his people. Now it's your turn to fully commit, heart and soul, to seeking your God. So get started—build the holy house of worship for God! Then you can bring the Ark of the Covenant and all the sacred items for worship into the temple built to honor God."

title: David's GOATED Temple Staffing Plan
paragraphs: So, when King David was getting really old, he made his son Solomon the new king over Israel.

At the same time, he gathered all the leaders of Israel, the priests, and the Levites. They counted up all the Levites who were thirty or older, and the total came out to a massive thirty-eight thousand men. David then split them into different work groups. He was like, “Okay, 24,000 of you are going to run the worship services in the temple. 6,000 of you will be officials and judges. 4,000 will be security guards, and the last 4,000 will be the praise band, worshiping God with the instruments I had made for this.”
David then organized the Levites into divisions based on the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

The Gershonites were Ladan and Shimei. Ladan's three sons were Jehiel, Zetham, and Joel. Shimei's three sons were Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran. These guys were the heads of Ladan's families. Shimei also had four other sons: Jahath, Ziza, Jeush, and Beriah. Jahath was the first, then Ziza. Jeush and Beriah didn't have a ton of sons, so they were just counted as one family with one job.

The four sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. Amram's sons were Aaron and Moses. Aaron was specially chosen to work in the Most Holy Place, to burn incense to God, serve Him, and bless in His name forever. This was a permanent gig for Aaron and his descendants. Moses and his sons were counted as part of the tribe of Levi.
The sons of Moses were Gershom and Eliezer. Gershom's first son was Shubael. Eliezer's first and only son was Rehabiah, but even though Eliezer only had one son, Rehabiah had a *lot* of sons.

Shelomith was Izhar's first son. Hebron had four sons: Jeriah, Amariah, Jahaziel, and Jekameam. Uzziel had two sons: Micah and Isshiah. The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi.
