Mahli's sons were Eleazar and Kish. Eleazar died without any sons, only daughters. Their cousins, the sons of Kish, married them. Mushi had three sons: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth.
These were all the descendants of Levi, twenty years and older, listed by their families and family heads. They were all part of the work crews that took care of the worship at God's temple.

David said, “Now that the God of Israel has given His people peace and made Jerusalem His forever home, the Levites don't have to carry the Tabernacle and all its furniture around anymore.” These last instructions from David were for the Levites who were twenty years old and up.

From then on, the Levites' job was to help Aaron's descendants with the worship in God's house. This meant taking care of the courtyards and rooms, keeping all the worship stuff clean, handling any extra tasks needed for the services, and providing the bread for the table, the flour for the Meal Offerings, and the unleavened wafers. They were in charge of all the baking, mixing, measuring, and weighing. They also had to be there for morning and evening prayers to thank and praise God, and at all the Whole-Burnt-Offerings on the Sabbath, New Moons, and festivals. They were on a regular schedule to serve God, with the exact number of people required for each task.
Basically, the Levites, working alongside Aaron's sons, were responsible for everything related to worship: the place, the schedule, and how it was all organized.

title: God's A-Team: The Official Temple Roster
paragraphs: So, here's the breakdown of Aaron's family, the OG priests. His sons were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. But plot twist—Nadab and Abihu died before their dad and didn't have any kids. So, Eleazar and Ithamar had to step up and take over the family business of being priests.

King David, being the organized guy he was, put Zadok from Eleazar's family and Ahimelech from Ithamar's family in charge of their own crews to handle their specific jobs. Turns out, Eleazar's family had way more leaders than Ithamar's, so they had to get the numbers right. They ended up with sixteen clan leaders from Eleazar's side and eight from Ithamar's.

To keep things fair and square, they basically drew straws to assign the leaders. No favoritism here! It was all legit, because there were high-ranking officials for both the sanctuary and for God in both families.

The secretary, a Levite named Shemaiah son of Nethanel, wrote down all the names with the king, the officials, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech son of Abiathar, and all the heads of the priestly and Levitical families watching. They took turns picking, one family from Eleazar, then one from Ithamar.

The first pick went to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah, third to Harim, fourth to Seorim, fifth to Malkijah, sixth to Mijamin, seventh to Hakkoz, eighth to Abijah, ninth to Jeshua, tenth to Shecaniah, eleventh to Eliashib, twelfth to Jakim, thirteenth to Huppah, fourteenth to Jeshebeab, fifteenth to Bilgah, sixteenth to Immer, seventeenth to Hezir, eighteenth to Happizzez, nineteenth to Pethahiah, twentieth to Jehezkel, twenty-first to Jakin, twenty-second to Gamul, twenty-third to Delaiah, and the twenty-fourth went to Maaziah.
That was the order they served in when they went into God's Temple, following the rules their ancestor Aaron had set up, just like God, the God of Israel, had told him to.
Now for the rest of the Levites:
From Amram's sons, there was Shubael; and from Shubael's sons, Jehdeiah.
From Rehabiah's crew, Isshiah was the top guy.
From the Izharites, there was Shelomoth; and from Shelomoth's sons, Jahath.
Hebron's sons were Jeriah (the first), Amariah (the second), Jahaziel (the third), and Jekameam (the fourth).
Uzziel's son was Micah, and from Micah's sons, Shamir. Micah's brother was Isshiah, and from Isshiah's sons, Zechariah.
The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi. Jaaziah's son was Beno. The sons of Merari from Jaaziah were Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.
From Mahli, there was Eleazar, who actually had no sons.
From Kish, there was Jerahmeel, Kish's son.
And from Mushi's sons, there were Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth.

These were all the Levites, listed by their families. They also cast lots, just like their relatives, Aaron's sons, did. King David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the leaders of the priestly and Levitical families were all there to see it. They treated the families of the oldest and youngest brothers exactly the same. No one got special treatment!

title: The Temple's GOATED Music Team
paragraphs: Alright, so David and the top worship leaders picked out a special crew from the families of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun. Their job? To prophesy and make music. It was a pretty big deal. Here’s the official lineup and what they did:

From Asaph's family, you had Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asarelah. They were all under their dad Asaph, who was basically God's mouthpiece, with the king's full backing. From Jeduthun's family, there were six sons: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Shimei, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah. Their dad, Jeduthun, was in charge. He'd prophesy while playing the zither—leading everyone in thanking and praising God. A total rockstar. Then there was Heman's family, and this family was huge: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shubael, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-Ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth. These were the sons of Heman, the king's own seer. They were his support system for the work God gave him. God blessed Heman with a wild fourteen sons and three daughters. Under their father’s supervision they were in charge of leading the singing and providing musical accompaniment in the work of worship in the sanctuary of God (Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman took their orders directly from the king). They were all pros, total masters of God's music. There were 288 of them.
To make it fair, they drew lots for their assignments. Didn't matter if you were old or young, a pro or a student—everyone got a fair shot. No special treatment.

The first name from Asaph’s family was Joseph and his twelve sons and brothers; second, Gedaliah and his twelve sons and brothers; third, Zaccur and his twelve sons and brothers; fourth, Izri and his twelve sons and brothers; fifth, Nethaniah and his twelve sons and brothers; sixth, Bukkiah and his twelve sons and brothers; seventh, Jesarelah and his twelve sons and brothers; eighth, Jeshaiah and his twelve sons and brothers; ninth, Mattaniah and his twelve sons and brothers; tenth, Shimei and his twelve sons and brothers; eleventh, Azarel and his twelve sons and brothers; twelfth, Hashabiah and his twelve sons and brothers; thirteenth, Shubael and his twelve sons and brothers; fourteenth, Mattithiah and his twelve sons and brothers; fifteenth, Jerimoth and his twelve sons and brothers; sixteenth, Hananiah and his twelve sons and brothers; seventeenth, Joshbekashah and his twelve sons and brothers; eighteenth, Hanani and his twelve sons and brothers; nineteenth, Mallothi and his twelve sons and brothers; twentieth, Eliathah and his twelve sons and brothers; twenty-first, Hothir and his twelve sons and brothers; twenty-second, Giddalti and his twelve sons and brothers; twenty-third, Mahazioth and his twelve sons and brothers; twenty-fourth, Romamti-Ezer and his twelve sons and brothers.

title: God's Temple Security Squad: The Ultimate Roster
paragraphs: So, the security team for the temple was from Korah's family. You had Meshelemiah, son of Kore (one of the sons of Asaph), and his seven sons: Zechariah the oldest, Jediael, Zebadiah, Jathniel, Elam, Jehohanan, and Eliehoenai. Then there was Obed-Edom's crew, and God totally blessed him with eight sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad, Joah, Sacar, Nethanel, Ammiel, Issachar, and Peullethai. Shemaiah's sons were legit leaders in the family: Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad, and his relatives Elihu and Semakiah were also pretty epic. These guys were all from Obed-Edom's line—total beasts, super strong and skilled. There were sixty-two of them. Meshelemiah had eighteen awesome sons and relatives. Hosah the Merarite's sons were Shimri (who wasn't the firstborn, but his dad made him the head), Hilkiah, Tabaliah, and Zechariah. Hosah had thirteen in his family.

These security teams, with their leaders calling the shots, kept everything in order at God's Temple, just like their ancestors did. They all got their assignments the same way, didn't matter how famous their families were—they basically drew their gate duty out of a hat. Shelemiah got the East Gate, and his son Zechariah, who was super smart, got the North Gate. Obed-Edom was assigned the South Gate, and his sons were on duty at the storehouse. Shuppim and Hosah were stationed at the West Gate and the Shalleketh Gate on the main road.

The guards were posted shoulder to shoulder: six Levites a day on the east, four a day on the north and south, and two at a time at the storehouse. Out in the open court to the west, four guards were on the road and two were at the court itself.
So yeah, these are the security teams from the families of Korah and Merari.

Other Levites were put in charge of the money for God's Temple. From Ladan's family (the Gershonites), you had Jehieli, and his sons Zetham and his brother Joel. They were the ones managing the finances for God's sanctuary.

From the Amramites, Izharites, Hebronites, and Uzzielites, there was Shubael, a descendant of Moses' son Gershom, who was the head financial guy. His relatives through Eliezer were also on the team: his son Rehabiah, his son Jeshaiah, his son Joram, his son Zicri, and his son Shelomith. Shelomith and his relatives were in charge of all the valuable stuff that King David, the family heads, and the army generals had dedicated. They took the loot they got from wars and dedicated it for the repair of God's temple. Plus, anything that had ever been dedicated by Samuel the seer, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah—all of it was Shelomith and his family's responsibility.

From the Izharite family, Kenaniah and his sons were appointed as officials and judges for stuff outside of the temple and worship. From the Hebronite family, Hashabiah and his relatives—1,700 really qualified guys—were in charge of the administration for both God's work and the king's work in the area west of the Jordan River.

According to the Hebronite family tree, Jeriah was the main guy. In the 40th year of King David's reign, they looked into the Hebronite family history and found some seriously impressive men over at Jazer in Gilead. These guys, Jeriah and 2,700 of his extended family, were put in charge by King David to handle all the administrative work for God and the king in the territory east of the Jordan—for the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

title: King David's A-Team: The Ultimate Roster
paragraphs: Alright, so here's the rundown of Israel's top guys, sorted by their family leaders, commanders, captains, and all the other officers who helped the king with military stuff. The army was split into divisions, and each division was on duty for one of the twelve months of the year. Every division had 24,000 soldiers.
First up, for the first month, was Jashobeam, son of Zabdiel. He was in charge of 24,000 men and came from Perez's family line. He was the head honcho over all the army officers for that first month.
The division for the second month was led by Dodai the Ahohite, with 24,000 men. Mikloth was the leader of his division.

The commander for the third month was Benaiah, son of Jehoiada the priest, with another 24,000 men. This is the same Benaiah who was one of the 'Mighty Men' in the top thirty and their chief. His son Ammizabad was in charge of the division.
Fourth division, fourth month: Asahel, Joab's brother. His son Zebadiah took over after him, leading 24,000 men.
Fifth division, fifth month: the commander was Shamhuth the Izrahite, with 24,000 men.
Sixth division, sixth month: Ira, son of Ikkesh the Tekoite, with 24,000 men.
Seventh division, seventh month: Helez the Pelonite, an Ephraimite, with 24,000 men.
Eighth division, eighth month: Sibbecai the Hushathite, a Zerahite, with 24,000 men.
Ninth division, ninth month: Abiezer the Anathothite, a Benjaminite, with 24,000 men.
Tenth division, tenth month: Maharai the Netophathite, a Zerahite, with 24,000 men.
Eleventh division, eleventh month: Benaiah the Pirathomite, an Ephraimite, with 24,000 men.
Twelfth division, twelfth month: Heldai the Netophathite from the family of Othniel, with 24,000 men.
Here are the guys in charge of the tribes' business:
for Reuben: Eliezer son of Zicri;
for Simeon: Shephatiah son of Maacah;
for Levi: Hashabiah son of Kemuel;
for Aaron: Zadok;
for Judah: Elihu, David’s brother;
for Issachar: Omri son of Michael;
for Zebulun: Ishmaiah son of Obadiah;
for Naphtali: Jerimoth son of Azriel;
for Ephraim: Hoshea son of Azaziah;
for one half-tribe of Manasseh: Joel son of Pedaiah;
for the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead: Iddo son of Zechariah;
for Benjamin: Jaasiel son of Abner;
for Dan: Azarel son of Jeroham.
These were the administrative officers for the tribes of Israel.

David didn't count the guys under twenty because God had promised to make Israel's population as huge as the stars in the sky. Joab, son of Zeruiah, started counting but never finished. God got seriously angry with Israel because of it. Turns out, the numbers were never even written down in King David's official records.
The king's storage facilities were managed by Azmaveth son of Adiel. Jonathan son of Uzziah was in charge of the warehouses in the outer areas.
Ezri son of Kelub was in charge of the farm workers.
Shimei the Ramathite was in charge of the vineyards, and Zabdi the Shiphmite was in charge of the grapes for the wine vats.
Baal-Hanan the Gederite was in charge of the olive and sycamore-fig trees in the western hills, and Joash was in charge of the olive oil.
Shitrai the Sharonite was in charge of the herds in Sharon, and Shaphat son of Adlai was in charge of the herds in the valley.
Obil the Ishmaelite was in charge of the camels, Jehdeiah the Meronothite was in charge of the donkeys, and Jaziz the Hagrite was in charge of the flocks.
These were the people responsible for taking care of King David’s property.
Jonathan, David’s uncle, who was a super wise and smart counselor, and Jehiel son of Hacmoni, were in charge of raising the king’s sons.
Ahithophel was the king’s counselor; Hushai the Arkite was the king’s close friend. Ahithophel was later replaced by Jehoiada son of Benaiah and by Abiathar.
Joab was the commander of the king’s army.

title: King David's GOATED Final Speech & Passing the Torch to Solomon
paragraphs: So David got all the big shots of Israel together—the heads of the tribes, the government department bosses, the army generals and captains, the guys who managed the king's and his sons' properties and animals—basically, everyone important in the kingdom.

King David stood up and was like, 'Listen up, my people. I was all in on building a forever home for the Ark of the Covenant, which is like God's footstool. But right when I was about to start, God told me, "Nah, you can't build a house for me. You've been in too many wars and have too much blood on your hands." It's wild, but God picked me from my whole family to be king over Israel for good. First, he picked the tribe of Judah to be in charge, then he zeroed in on my family, and out of all my dad's sons, he chose me. He was actually happy to make me king over all of Israel. Then, out of all my sons—and trust me, God gave me a bunch—he picked my son Solomon to take over the throne of God's kingdom in Israel. God also said, "Your son Solomon is the one who will build my house and my courts. I've chosen him as my own son, and I'll be his father. I'll make sure his kingdom is solid, but only if he stays focused on following my commands and decisions, just like he is right now.'

'So now, with everyone in Israel watching and God listening, I'm telling you as God's people: you gotta obey and really get to know all of God's commands. That way, you can enjoy this awesome land and pass it down to your kids, making sure they have a good future.'

'And you, Solomon my son, for real, get to know your dad's God. Serve him with your whole heart and a willing mind, because God checks out every heart and knows what's up with every motive. If you look for him, he'll make sure you find him, but if you ditch him, he'll be out for good. So pay attention! God has chosen you to build his holy house. Be brave, be determined! And get it done!'

Then David gave his son Solomon the blueprints for the whole Temple area: the porch, the storage rooms, the meeting rooms, and the special spot for the atonement sacrifice. He handed over all the plans that God's Spirit had put in his head: the design for the courtyards, how the rooms should be set up, and the closets for all the holy items. He gave him the plan for how the Levites and priests should be organized for their work, leading worship in God's house and taking care of all the stuff used in the services. He laid out the exact amounts of gold and silver needed for every single item used in worship: the gold and silver lampstands and lamps, the gold tables for the holy bread, the silver tables, the gold forks, bowls, and jars, and the Incense Altar. And he gave him the design for the cherubim statues with their wings spread out over the Ark of the Covenant—the cherubim throne. David said, 'Here are the blueprints for the whole project, just as God made me understand it.'

David kept talking to Solomon: 'Take charge! Be confident! Don't get stressed or discouraged. God, my God, is with you on this; he won't abandon you or leave you hanging. He's by your side until every last detail for God's worship service is finished. You've got all the priests and Levites ready to help out, and all sorts of skilled craftsmen and artisans ready to get to work. The leaders and the people are all on board. Just give the word.'

title: David's Mic Drop Moment & Solomon's Coronation
paragraphs: Then King David stood up in front of everyone and said, “So, God handpicked my son Solomon for this huge project. He’s young and still has a lot to learn, and this job is massive—we’re not just building a community center, this is a house for God to meet with us. I’ve literally done everything I can to get the materials ready for my God’s house: gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, all kinds of precious and colorful stones, and massive piles of building stones. On top of that, because I’m so passionate about this, I’m throwing in my own personal fortune of gold and silver for God’s temple. We’re talking 3,000 talents of the best gold from Ophir (about 113 tons!) and 7,000 talents of silver (214 tons!) to cover the walls and for all the fancy detail work the artists will do.
“So now it’s your turn. Who’s ready to step up and give big for God?”

And you won’t believe it, they were totally ready. The leaders of the families, the chiefs of the tribes, the army commanders, and the king’s managers all stepped up and gave generously. They donated 5,000 talents of gold (188 tons!), 10,000 darics of gold (185 pounds!), 10,000 talents of silver (377 tons!), 18,000 talents of bronze (679 tons!), and a wild 100,000 talents of iron (3,775 tons!). And anyone who had rare jewels gave them to the treasury of the Temple of God, which was managed by Jehiel the Gershonite.
The people were so hyped—everyone was giving with such a good attitude, totally willingly and freely! And King David? He was absolutely ecstatic.
Then David praised God in front of everyone:

“We praise you, God of our ancestor Israel, from forever ago to forever in the future. You, O God, are the greatest, the most powerful, the most glorious, the ultimate winner, and the most majestic. Everything in the sky and on earth is yours! The kingdom is all yours! You’re lifted high above everything. Riches and honor come straight from you, you rule over everything. You’ve got all the strength and power to build people up and make them strong. So here we are, our God, just saying thank you and praising your awesome name.

“But for real, who am I, and who are my people, that we could even think of giving you anything? Everything comes from you in the first place; we’re just giving you back what you already gave us. From your perspective, we’re just like our ancestors—homeless, aimless wanderers, here one day and gone the next, like a shadow. There’s not much to us. Our God, all this stuff we’ve piled up to build a house to honor your holy name—it all came from you! It was yours to begin with! I know, dear God, that you don’t care about appearances—you want the real us, our true hearts. So I’ve given all this with a happy and honest heart. And now, look at all these people doing the same thing, giving freely and willingly—it’s such a joy to see! O God, the God of our fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, please keep this generous spirit alive in your people forever. Keep their hearts locked in on you. And give my son Solomon a clear and focused mind so he can follow all your commands and instructions, and actually build the temple that I’ve prepared for.”
Then David told the crowd, “Now, praise your God!” And they all did it. They praised God, the God of their ancestors, and bowed down to worship God and the king.

The very next day, they had a massive barbecue for God. They sacrificed a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, and a thousand sheep, plus drink offerings and a bunch of other sacrifices. They feasted all day, eating and drinking in God’s presence, just totally full of joy.

Then they had a second coronation for Solomon, officially making him the leader in God’s eyes, and they anointed Zadok as the priest. Solomon sat on God’s throne as king, taking over from his dad David. And everything went smoothly; all of Israel listened to him. All the leaders, even all of King David’s other sons, pledged their loyalty to King Solomon. God made Solomon a superstar, giving him more fame and honor than any king in Israel before him.

So, David, son of Jesse, ruled over all of Israel. He was king for 40 years—7 years in Hebron and 33 in Jerusalem. He died old and happy, with a long life, lots of money, and a great reputation. His son Solomon took over after him. The whole story of King David, from beginning to end, is written down in the records of Samuel the seer, Nathan the prophet, and Gad the seer. It covers his entire rule, all his epic adventures, and everything that happened with him, Israel, and the kingdoms around them.
